main_text.p: tium conditione, variari solet multipliciter, secundum qualitates primas, secundas &c. exempli causa secundum primas, quando in simplici non datur gradus quem cupimus, sed aut remissior, aut intensior. Cupio calidum in secundo gradu, nec datur simplex conveniens, cogor addere aliud simplex: sed hoc opus hic labor, in proportione invenienda; de eâ enim dubitatur; rectius ii sentiunt, qui gradus alterantium ex effectibus sensui manifestis constituunt: nimirum ut gradus æquales constituantur, hoc enim modo temperatum medicamentum, habebit æquales partes caloris, frigoris, humiditatis, & siccitatis. Nempe si summus in temperatis gradus sit sex, tres erunt gradus caloris, & totidem frigoris. in intemperatis, tantum unius contrarii corrumpi debet, quantum alterius generari. Ergo calidum in primo est, quod uno gradu superat temperatum; in secundo, quod duobus superat, & ita deinceps. Frigidum in secundo
Note: the marginal notes on the left edge are too faint and cut off to be read reliably.

page.notes: The left margin notes are cut off by the binding and are not legible; they are not transcribed. The text of the first line is a continuation from the previous page. Some words such as "conveniens," and "sed" are read with reasonable but not complete certainty; the ligature forms of long s have been normalised to s.
